subject: Discovery recap: migrating off proprietary LLM APIs (FinPay)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@finpay.com>, Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: migrating off proprietary LLM APIs (FinPay)

Hi Sara / Miguel 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we're aligned. Please correct anything I've missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-token spend with current OpenAI/Anthropic pipelines (esp. embeddings + chat).
- Vendor lock-in risk and limited control over model versions and inference behavior.
- Compliance constraints around logging, retention, and customer data isolation for regulated payments data.
- Latency spikes during peak trading windows that affect real-time features.

Current stack (what you told us):
- Generation/chat: OpenAI Chat Completions (proxying via internal API gateway).
- Safety / guardrails: Anthropic for safety checks on certain flows.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings used for semantic search / retrieval.
- Orchestration: In-house microservice that fans out calls and aggregates responses.

Success criteria for migration (explicit):
1) Model parity: generation and embeddings quality within acceptable deltas versus OpenAI/Anthropic for your top-10 intents.
2) Latency: 95th percentile within 20% of current production for core flows.
3) Cost: target ~30% unit cost reduction on inference for primary workloads.
4) Compliance: ability to run in a private deployment (VPC / customer-controlled keys) and provide audit logs.
5) Compatibility: support function-calling-style structured outputs and a drop-in compatibility surface for your existing API layer.

Model shortlist we discussed (initial):
- Llama 2 / fine-tuned variants (good baseline for generation).
- Mistral-Inference / Mistral-large for high throughput on encoder-decoder tasks.
- Falcon-40B / Falcon variants for embeddings and chat.
- Mixtral / instruction-tuned efficient models for cost-sensitive paths.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rishi/Aditya: deliver a 4-week POC plan + success metrics doc (scope attached).
2) FinPay: share example prompt sets + top-10 intents, and a small evaluation dataset (200 examples) for quality validation.
3) Align on infra constraints: whether you need on-prem vs. VPC private deployment and KMS/HSM requirements.
4) Schedule POC kickoff next week suggested times: Tue/Wed morning PT.

Attachments: POC-scope.pdf (draft), Redwood compatibility matrix spreadsheet.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the POC scope.

Thanks,
Rishi
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@finpay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@finpay.com>, Aaron Chen <aaron.chen@finpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 16:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migrating off proprietary LLM APIs (FinPay)

Thanks Rishi this looks right to us.

A couple clarifications / notes:
- For compliance, we will need support for customer-managed KMS and the ability to truncate or redact specific fields from logs. We can share the redaction policy separately.
- For embeddings, we rely heavily on similarity thresholds for fraud signals any change in embedding space needs to be measurable in your eval.
- On success criteria #1 (model parity), can you call out what pass/fail thresholds you plan to use? We'll want to review before the POC starts.

We'll get you the 200-example eval set by Monday. Tue morning PT works for a kickoff.

Sara
Head of ML Infrastructure
FinPay

On Sat, Feb 20, 2027 at 4:05 PM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> (original message)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 16:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migrating off proprietary LLM APIs (FinPay)

Sara good questions. Quick answers inline and a few follow-ups: 

- KMS / redaction: we support customer-managed keys in our Private deployment and have configurable log retention / redact pipelines. We'll include the exact retention and redaction hooks in the POC doc.

- Embeddings evaluation: our POC plan will include a set of quantitative metrics (cosine similarity distributions, MRR on retrieval tasks, precision@k for fraud labeling) plus qualitative review for the top 10 intents. If the embedding shift causes >5% regression on any critical metric we'll iterate model/quantization choices.

- Pass/fail thresholds: propose we start with "no more than 7% drop in generation quality per intent on automatic metrics (BLEU/ROUGE for templated outputs + human-rated NPS for conversational quality) and <=5% regression on core embedding metrics". We'll document this and you can edit.

Next questions:
1) Do you have specific latency SLOs (absolute numbers) for the flows we should target, or is % delta relative to current acceptable?
2) For peak load testing, can you share the 99th percentile token/sec that we should emulate?

I'll attach the POC scope and a compatibility matrix (sent in follow-up email).

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>

Looping in a couple of implementation notes from our side before the kickoff:

- Aditya: can you confirm resource estimates (GPU type / memory) for the shortlisted models and a fast estimate for batch sizes we should design for?
- Rishi: I'll prepare a short checklist for the POC that includes data access agreements, test harness, evaluation rubric, and rollback criteria.
- Sara / Miguel: we'll send a calendar invite for Tue 10:00 AM PT and include a 30-minute agenda: intro, scope walkthrough, evaluation metrics, and infra constraints.

Marissa

Redwood Inference
